Validation

Source: vignettes/articles/validation.Rmd
validation.Rmd

Every statistic of AgriDesign is checked against an independent implementation: functions of base R, established R packages, worked examples of textbooks and software manuals, and closed-form results. The checks are scripts in the validation/ folder of the source repository; each prints one line per comparison and the number of checks passed. At the time of writing all 540 checks pass. The package itself depends on no other package: the reference packages are used only by these scripts.

Script Checks Compared with
v01-anova.R 29 aov() with Error() strata, car (Type III), emmeans, agricolae (sp.plot)
v02-assumptions-nonpar.R 38 shapiro.test, nortest, car (Levene, Durbin-Watson), MASS (boxcox), friedman.test, kruskal.test, oneway.test, PMCMRplus, ARTool, rcompanion
v03-means.R 47 TukeyHSD, pairwise.t.test, agricolae, mvtnorm, PMCMRplus, emmeans, lmerTest
v04-figures.R 17 the numbers of each analysis against what is drawn; file formats and resolution
v05-generator.R 31 structure over many seeds, uniformity tests, power.t.test
v06-report.R 30 the figures of the analysis in the HTML, well-formed and self-contained pages
v07a-designs.R 63 closed forms of efficiency factors, agricolae designs, lme4 + emmeans (REML)
v07b-breeding.R 199 agricolae, lm, svd, lme4, exact enumeration of F2 populations and of rank distributions
v07c-tests-pathology.R 86 a SAS manual example, an independent double integral, PMCMRplus, chisq.test, fisher.test, agricolae

Differences with other software

When two programs disagree, the validation looks for a third, independent answer. These differences were found, and in each case the reason is stated in the validation script:

  • Dunnett’s critical value. With its default tolerance, multcomp computes the multivariate t by quasi-Monte Carlo with an error of about 1e-3 (2.7251 instead of 2.7273 for four comparisons and 15 error degrees of freedom). AgriDesign integrates it with Gauss-Legendre quadrature, using the exact correlation of every pair, and agrees with mvtnorm at high precision.
  • Efficiency of alpha designs. agricolae::design.alpha() prints the upper bound of Patterson and Williams as the efficiency factor of the design it builds. For 12 treatments in blocks of 3 with 2 replicates it prints 0.6471, while its layout has an efficiency of 0.5946.
  • Latin squares. Permuting the rows, columns and symbols of a cyclic square reaches only 432 of the 576 Latin squares of order 4. AgriDesign draws them uniformly with the Jacobson-Matthews chain.
  • North Carolina design III. The dominance variance equals the males x testers component; doubling it (as agricolae does) overestimates it by a factor of two, as the exact enumeration of an F2 population shows.
  • Line x tester. The average covariance of half-sibs needs the factor (l + t - 2) of the weighted mean square, the covariance of full-sibs keeps every term of the formula of Singh and Chaudhary, and the dominance variance is 4 sigma2_SCA / (1 + F)^2.
  • Huehn’s S(1). Its variance includes the factor (K^2 - 1) / K^2, as the exact null distribution confirms.
  • Waller-Duncan. The critical t agrees with the SAS manual example and with an independent double integral; agricolae’s approximation drifts when the treatments have one degree of freedom or when F is large.
  • Median test. agricolae::Median.test(correct = TRUE) does not apply the continuity correction, because the argument reaches chisq.test() in the wrong position.
  • van der Waerden test. Rounding the ranks to three decimals before the normal scores changes the statistic in the fourth significant digit.
  • Power. A shifted central t underestimates the power with few error degrees of freedom (0.21 instead of 0.245 for a CV of 15 %, a difference of 15 % and four replicates); AgriDesign uses the noncentral t.
